transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (RiverMark Head of ML), Lena (RiverMark SRE), Tom (RiverMark Product)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy valentines but more importantly the weekly poc sync, do we have any last-minute additions to the agenda?
[00:10] Samir: no, this looks good, main thing is the TTFT numbers from last week and Maya's kernel suggestions
[00:15] Maya: yep i ran the basic experiments, i've got a couple of slides but i'll just walk through the numbers first, cool?
[00:22] Tom: sounds good
[00:25] Jordan: quick note - we'll try to keep to 45, we know folks have afternoon stuff

--- Summary recap / Context ---
[02:00] Jordan: recap, goal is reduce TTFT for first token to under 120ms on 1k sequences and keep 95th pct below 600ms for your critical route, right Samir?
[02:10] Samir: yes that's the target, for chat prompts we ideally want sub 100 on small queries but we know 4k is tougher
[02:18] Lena: also remember infra constraint - our KMS rotates keys monthly and the HSM policy disallows export, so TLS mutual auth and KMS handshake latency matter

--- Experiments and results ---
[05:30] Maya: ok so i compared three profiles: hosted baseline (no streaming), hosted with streaming enabled, and a dedicated pool with pinned kernels. For 1k sequence our baseline TTFT median was ~140ms, streaming pushed median down to 90-110ms depending on the chunk size; 95th pct improved from ~520ms to ~420ms.
[05:55] Samir: wait you said median 90-110, that's a range from chunk size? can you clarify
[06:02] Maya: yeah so when we stream in 64-token chunks the server can start sending earlier, you get faster first byte but you pay a bit in overall tail because of scheduling; with 128 chunk it's a little slower TTFT but slightly better overall throughput.
[06:20] Tom: is there any noticeable hallucination or output truncation with streaming on? we had seen truncated outputs on another stack
[06:28] Maya: good question - for our models i tested the streaming assembly logic and didn't see truncation, but if you do streaming plus eager decoding with weird stop tokens you can see edge cases; we'll include tests for your stop token set.

[08:00] Maya: for 4k seq the story is different: baseline TTFT for dedicated pinned kernels was about 280ms median, streaming brought it down to around 210ms but 95th still around 1.1s on our test harness at low concurrency. The main factor was kernel selection for long sequences - certain attention kernels blow up on memory copies and cause spikes.
[08:30] Jordan: can you say which kernels? like cuBLAS vs fused attention or the newer causal attention kernels?
[08:36] Maya: we saw the fused multi-head attention path and the tiled attention both behave differently - on A100 style hardware the fused kernel is faster for 1k and under, but for 4k the tiled kernel with better cache locality and async memcpy did better at tail. Our runtime will auto-select but you can pin kernel groups per model.
[09:00] Samir: we run on a mix of VMs that are mostly V100 equivalent for now in prod - will that change things?
[09:07] Maya: yes V100 tends to favor different kernel choices; i'll add a V100 profile, the tuned kernels we used were on A100/NVIDIA H100 sim but i can re-run on V100-like config.

--- Deep dive: TTFT and scheduling ---
[12:15] Maya: TTFT is affected by 1) model load time (cold start), 2) KV cache warmup, 3) scheduler queuing for batch formation, and 4) chunk size for streaming. For your workload cold starts are rare since Dedicated pools keep warmed models, but we saw queuing spikes with mixed small and large requests.
[12:45] Lena: that queuing is our concern, we have bursty traffic during biz hours, and we cannot accept big P95 regressions
[12:50] Jordan: one mitigation is route-level autoscaling and separate pools for short vs long sequences. That way small requests don't wait behind big 4k jobs.
[13:05] Samir: is that something Redwood can set up in the poc? we don't want to commit to Dedicated yet but want to test routing policy
[13:10] Maya: yes we can set routing rules in the POC - we can split by route header or by sequence_length heuristic. For the POC i suggest: Route A = <=1k, Route B = >1k. Keep them on same Dedicated pool but different instance grouping to avoid head-of-line blocking.

[15:00] Maya: i also tested quantization mixes - 4-bit mixed quant gave similar median but worse tail in some cases on our runtime. Mixed precision plus kernel pinning helped in one config but made TTFT for first token slightly worse because of extra dequant steps. So tradeoff there.
[15:20] Samir: we care more about stable tail than absolute median so maybe we accept a 10-20ms hit on median to shrink tail by 200ms
[15:28] Jordan: that's a common tradeoff, and it's aligned with your product SLOs. We'll tune for tail stability.

--- Streaming specifics and tradeoffs ---
[18:00] Maya: streaming will cut TTFT by starting earlier, but it increases number of small writes and can increase CPU overhead on the host for network IO. On dedicated infra with proper kernel choice streaming is net positive. For hosted we can enable streaming but watch for cost increase due to more calls/logging.
[18:30] Lena: network egress is also a cost and compliance point for us - we need per-request audit logs and tracing, streaming multiplies log events, will that be a problem?
[18:40] Jordan: we can batch logs at the collector to reduce events; also Redwood Console supports trace sampling, we can dial that to keep compliance while controlling log volumes.

[21:00] Tom: about kernel pinning - what does that look like operationally? will we lose the auto-fallback?
[21:10] Maya: you can pin kernel preferences at model version level; the runtime still supports fallback if pinned kernel fails but you get deterministic behavior. For the poc we can try pinning the tiled kernel for long sequences and fused for short ones.
[21:25] Samir: and quantization? we prefer Q4 for cost but only if tail is stable
[21:30] Maya: right, Q4 can save tokens and memory but increases dequant/quant steps, so for RLHF-like prompts with many short responses Q4 is fine. For long seq generation with heavy attention we saw tail spikes so maybe use Q8 or mixed for >2k sequences.

[24:00] Lena: can you share exact commands? our infra team wants to reproduce locally, not rely on Redwood console only
[24:10] Maya: sure, i'll share a runbook with the runtime flags, kernel group names, and the exact batch/queue settings we used. Also i'll share the perf CSVs and the small Jupyter notebook we used to generate the charts.
[24:25] Jordan: we'll attach those to the next email and put them in the shared drive link.

--- Questions from customer ---
[28:00] Samir: a few questions - 1) Will enabling streaming affect model determinism for evals? 2) If we do route split, do we pay double for model memory? 3) How does this affect caching semantics?
[28:12] Maya: 1) streaming doesn't change model outputs deterministically if you keep decoding settings identical; it's a transport change. 2) Route split on same pool can reuse the same model instance in memory, it's more about scheduler isolation than memory duplication unless you pin to different GPUs. 3) caching: prefix/KV cache works per model version; streaming doesn't affect KV semantics, but with chunked decoding you may warm cache differently.
[29:00] Samir: good, 3 more quick ones - will you include a V100 profile, and can you run a 95th pct test with 100 concurrent users? we need that number for our infra review.
[29:08] Maya: yes to both, i'll run V100-like simulation and schedule the 100-concurrent benchmark for next week, but need your prompt sets.

[31:00] Jordan: quick note on security - we heard from Lena earlier about KMS rotation. For Dedicated we can integrate your KMS, and the Redwood Private control plane supports HSM-backed keys but we need to confirm rotation window doesn't break token signing. Lena will confirm.
[31:20] Lena: we'll validate, i think monthly rotation might require a short maintenance window for signing key swap - i'll confirm with infra and let you know.

--- Wrap and next steps ---
[38:45] Jordan: ok recap - Maya runs TTFT+streaming experiments for both 1k and 4k, include V100 profile and pinned kernel variants; Samir provide prompt sets; Jordan sends kernel notes and Dedicated pricing and the runbook; Lena confirms KMS constraints. We'll meet same time next week to review results.
[39:10] Tom: works for me, thanks
[39:15] Samir: thanks everyone
[39:20] Jordan: thanks all, i'll send calendar invite and notes

[44:30] (call ends)
